newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: GOLF-BALLESTEROS VOWS TO PLAY ON.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-BALLESTEROS VOWS TO PLAY ON.

text.p: Ryder Cup captain Severiano Ballesteros vowed to play his way through his problems after soaring to a 78 at the Irish Open on Friday and missing his ninth cut in 11 events this year.
But while his own confidence may have gone astray, fellow Spaniard Jose Maria Olazabal came out firmly on the side of his compatriot's ability to sort out his game and become a winner again.

After a first round 75, Ballesteros had disclosed that he will not try to be a playing captain against Tom Kite's Americans at Valderrama in September because of the state of his game and the condition of his back.
On Friday Ballesteros vowed: "I play on. I've never been one to quit and I never will. I will play out of this."
Olazabal, who played both rounds with his friend, agreed.
"It was not at all nice to see Seve hitting the ball like that," said Olazabal after witnessing a double-bogey and seven bogeys as Ballesteros missed the cut by seven strokes on 153, 11 over par.
"He is going through such a bad spell and he has to regroup and start from scratch with his game.

"But the competitive desire is still there and I saw it over both days. I'm confident that somehow he will get his game back and I firmly believe he will win again because he still has the ability, especially with his short game.
"I've been in the same situation and you just have to try to hold on to your self-belief and know that sooner or later a bad spell will pass.
"But I know it's difficult saying anything to him, and the best thing is just to offer support whenever it's wanted," Olazabal said."
The third member of their group, Irishman Paul McGinley, added: "You can see how much it is hurting him, the fact that he can't compete any more.
"His biggest asset is his short game and because he is getting into so much trouble off the tee, he isn't able to use it."
Ballesteros will play in next week's Loch Lomond Invitational before going on to Royal Troon for the British Open, which he has won three times in the past.
